title: Lawmakers look to avoid government shutdown, and reconsider getting rid of them entirely
summary: The latest proposals would change how Congress handles funding lapses and could reshape the budget fights that have repeatedly disrupted federal operations.

title: Despite firings, acting IG says it’s 'the best time to be in the inspector general community' due to focus on fraud
summary: A panel of inspectors general at a government accounting conference also discussed challenges combating technologically advanced scams and performing more proactive oversight.

title: Unions ask for injunction restoring collective bargaining at Defense
summary: The latest filing from a pair of federal employee unions highlights the ways in which the Pentagon strayed from the Trump administration’s own guidance for implementing the president’s executive order banning collective bargaining at most agencies on national security grounds.

title: ICE ramps up arrests as deportation effort expands
summary: New data reflects the administration's push to increase enforcement while judges continue scrutinizing some of its detention policies.

title: Inspector general group would be axed under new House GOP bill
summary: Supporters of the measure pointed to a recent Government Accountability Office report that found the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency frequently missed requirements when investigating misconduct allegations against IGs.

title: Former Education officials warn agency transfers could undermine core functions
summary: Officials from Republican and Democratic administrations said moving key responsibilities outside the department could create confusion and erode oversight.

title: CDC shifts HIV prevention funds away from groups tackling this work
summary: The health agency will route HIV prevention grants through state and local health departments instead of directly funding community-based organizations.

title: OPM moves to implement long-awaited retirement fix for federal first responders
summary: The First Responders Fair RETIRE Act, which ensures federal workers can stay on accelerated mandatory retirement schedules even if they transfer to another due to injury, was signed into law in 2022.

title: Transportation looks to AI to accelerate its modernization initiatives
summary: Steven Bradbury, the agency’s deputy secretary, said AI has helped Transportation slash its software production timeline from 18 months down to 18 weeks.

title: Homan says ICE officers will wear body cameras during traffic stops
summary: The move follows two fatal shootings this month as the administration continues aggressive immigration enforcement.

title: OPM shrinks its workforce by a third, seeks further staffing cuts
summary: The agency is giving employees in its healthcare and insurance division another shot at opting into the deferred resignation program.

title: Arbitrator restores telework for IRS workers
summary: The Internal Revenue Service withdrew from participating in the National Treasury Employees Union’s grievance against the agency for its 2025 return-to-office push in March, forcing independent arbitrator Christopher Shulman to conduct proceedings with management in absentia.

title: Secret Service is examining apparent Iranian video outlining Trump motorcade routes, assassination opportunities
summary: The agency said it is looking into the Persian-language video, which uses polished, apparently AI-generated graphics to depict supposed motorcade routes in Florida and New York.

title: Traffic stops become a flashpoint in ICE shootings
summary: A review found nearly all shootings involving federal immigration officers since Trump's return to office began with vehicle enforcement, a tactic the administration briefly paused before resuming.

title: Energy Department removes more than 1,600 webpages from public website
summary: The agency has taken down consumer energy resources without explaining why, the latest example of changes to public-facing federal information under the Trump administration.

title: GSA wants other agencies to borrow what's working on tech
summary: After testing successful approaches internally, the agency is inviting federal employees across government to see how they can apply them in their own organizations.

title: How a little-known Trump directive reshaped the government's counterterrorism approach
summary: COMMENTARY | A presidential national security memorandum has become the framework for investigations and prosecutions that critics say raise new questions about executive power and civil liberties.

title: Labor nominee defends administration’s strategy for shifting Education Department work
summary: Keith Sonderling argued the Labor Department is providing administrative support, not taking over policy, as Democrats questioned whether moving education programs across agencies will improve outcomes.

title: Pentagon closes cyber apprenticeship applications early after receiving over 15,000
summary: A Defense Department official told Nextgov/FCW that the agency is “rolling out additional apprenticeship positions over the next few weeks.”

title: Trump stretches declassified China intelligence into broader 2020 election claims
summary: The records provide new details about Chinese intelligence collection on voters and internal analytic debates, but do not undercut longstanding findings on the 2020 election.

title: House GOP cancels VA overhaul vote again
summary: House Republicans narrowly defeated a motion that would have sent the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act back to committee but has struggled to build support for its counter to a looming discharge petition to advance another bill aimed at increasing veterans’ benefits.
